All data is 100% public with zero authentication barriers — no web scraping of password-protected portals, no purchased private datasets. Direct bulk downloads or simple form-based queries available from all sources, making this a low-to-moderate engineering lift with zero legal risk.

engineering_notes: Aggregate state oil & gas operator registries (Texas RRC bulk download, North Dakota operator list, Oklahoma Corporation Commission, Colorado ECMC, Wyoming OGCC, New Mexico EMNRD, Louisiana DNR) via direct downloads or form-based queries — all public, zero authentication. Cross-reference with EPA TRI facility database (bulk CSV download at data.epa.gov) filtering for petroleum refineries and petrochemical plants (NAICS 324110, 325110). Scrape EPA NPDES permit database for refinery wastewater permits. Parse SEC EDGAR 10-K filings for publicly traded energy companies (ExxonMobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, EOG, Pioneer, Occidental, Kinder Morgan, Energy Transfer, Williams) extracting executive contacts and facility locations from Exhibit 21 subsidiaries and Item 2 properties disclosures. Download EIA electricity generator database filtering for wind/solar (fuel type codes WND, SUN). Normalize company names (handle 'LLC' vs 'L.L.C.', 'Incorporated' vs 'Inc.'), geocode facility addresses, classify sector (upstream/midstream/downstream/services/renewable) via NAICS and facility type keywords, deduplicate multi-state operators by matching parent company names and addresses. Enrich missing emails via domain pattern matching (info@companyname.com, contact@companyname.com) and business directory lookups (ZoomInfo, Apollo, Hunter.io for company domain verification). Estimated engineering time: 40-60 hours (moderate complexity due to multi-source aggregation, but all sources are clean public databases with structured data, not unstructured web scraping).
compliance_notes: Zero PII — all data is company-level business information (corporate legal names, operator numbers, facility addresses, business phone/email publicly listed in regulatory filings for permitting and compliance purposes). State oil & gas operator registries are public records under state open records laws and FOIA. EPA TRI and NPDES databases are federally mandated public disclosures under Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA) and Clean Water Act — no privacy restrictions. SEC filings are public domain. Industry association directories publish member names for networking and business development. Contact information (phone, email) is publicly disclosed by energy companies themselves for permitting, regulatory compliance, and commercial purposes — no expectation of privacy. No GDPR applicability (US energy companies, not EU individuals). Automatic PASS expected from compliance-officer — no sensitive data, all regulatory/business disclosures.
